title: Occupancy-based Quantile Risk Control
claim: A sequential procedure partitions the loss space, samples test-loss occupancy across bins, then computes a risk bound to select the optimal parameter.
layout: Top search loop above 3 left-to-right stage panels, math inside boxes
description: A wide pipeline diagram. A top row shows an outer loop: λ Candidate Λ feeds 'Next λ in Λ', then 'Compute Risk Bound', then a decision box 'R⁺(λ) ≤ α?'. 'Yes' exits to Optimal λ*, and 'No' loops back through an arrow over the top. A large rounded container below, titled 'Occupancy-based Quantile Risk Control (For Fixed λ)', expands the Compute Risk Bound step. At left, dot clusters for the calibration set (n known losses) and the test set (m unknown losses) feed in. Three colored panels run left to right: PARTITIONING (blue), where the loss axis from L to U is split into n+1 intervals by ordered losses X(0)...X(n+1). SAMPLING (teal), where counts N0...Nn sum to m and follow a uniform distribution. COMPUTING (green), where the risk measure and Φ⁺ function give a risk bound from B sampled risk values and a (1-δ) quantile histogram. Black arrows connect the stages, and the eye starts at the top loop and then moves to the three panel headers.
caption: Overview of Occupancy-based Quantile Risk Control. Given a risk level α and confidence 1 −δ, our OQRC implements a sequential procedure that calibrates a parameter λ∗of the ML model such that the quantile risk Rtest satisfies P(Rtest(λ∗) ≤α) ≥1 −δ.
abstract: Conformal risk control is an emerging framework for the safe deployment of machine learning models with finite-sample guarantees. To accommodate a broader class of risk notions, quantile risk control extends this framework to quantile-based risk measures. However, existing methods either suffer from excessive conservatism or lack rigorous finite-sample guarantees. To address these limitations, we introduce Occupancy-based Quantile Risk Control (OQRC), a novel method that provides tight risk control bounds with finite-sample validity. Our key idea is to formulate risk control as a finite-occupancy problem by partitioning the loss space with the ordered calibration losses. Specifically, we estimate the distribution of test losses across the resulting bins and upper-bound the risk by the maximum loss attained within each bin. We then select the parameter $Î»$ such that this upper bound does not exceed a predefined threshold $Î±$ with high probability $1-Î´$. Theoretically, we establish a finite-sample guarantee showing that OQRC yields tight risk control bounds that converge to the optimal bounds at a provable rate of $\mathcal{O}_ p(n^{-1/2})$. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our method, reducing the risk gap by up to 78.64\% on common benchmarks.
